limits: Only the GLB's own data is read: no renders, no source .blend, no textures decoded beyond image headers.
Mesh roles are name/geometry heuristics (inferred.meshRoles), not artist labels.
Each mesh is counted once even if several nodes instance it (instanceCount is reported).
H is the Y extent of ALL meshes (hair, props and footwear included); a prop above the head would inflate it.
Facing direction and handedness conventions are inferred from mask/joint placement when available, else from the glTF spec.

headTopSkin.basis: highest vertex of the body (skin) mesh; hair adds above it

neck.basis: narrowest central silhouette width between 0.65 H and the skin top minus 0.06 H (band centre; band height = H/100)

chin.basis: lowest central vertex above the neck whose z lies >= neck-front + 0.5 neck widths in front of the neck (the jaw leaving the neck in side view)

shoulderLine.basis: knee (max of normalised width-gain minus normalised descent) of the outer half-width profile between the neck and the widest band, or the widest band itself when the profile is a step (method: profile-knee)

armpit.basis: apex of the highest empty gap between torso cluster and arm cluster searching down from the shoulder line

chest.basis: band of maximum torso front-z between the waist and the shoulder line (bust/pectoral prominence)

waist.basis: band of minimum torso-cluster width between the hip maximum and the armpit

hips.basis: band of maximum torso-cluster width in the lower half between crotch and armpit

crotch.basis: top edge of the highest band, contiguous from the leg bottoms, with no vertex within 0.003 H of the midline (apex of the inter-leg gap)

knee.basis: peak of the smoothed rear-z profile (popliteal hollow) in the middle of the leg, at least 0.012 H above the calf bulge

limits: ankle: the leg cross-section has no constriction with a flare below it inside the skin mesh (the skin mesh may end above the ankle and hand over to separate foot/shoe meshes); ankle is null
mouth: no central detail mesh below the eyes; the mouth is probably painted in the texture atlas or modelled in the skin mesh, so mouth centre and corners are null
Silhouette bands see only vertex positions and triangle edges: surface detail between them, back detail, and cavities (inside the mouth, behind the ears) are not measured.
Head depth and shape under hair are those of the skin mesh; hair volume is reported separately (head.observed.withAllMeshesBounds) and the skull beneath it is not known.

Whether eyes, brows, lashes and mouth are geometry or painted cannot be told from the skin silhouette; separate detail meshes and mirrored twin islands of the skin mesh (inferred.embeddedPairedIslands) are reported, and their roles are guesses from size and position.
Landmarks are silhouette heuristics at band resolution (H/100); they are not anatomical bone landmarks.
Arm/torso separation uses a gap rule on folded |x|; arms pressed against the torso are merged into it.
The +z facing is assumed (glTF forward) and only cross-checked against the face-detail meshes.
Texel densities and atlas colours describe the atlas as authored; they do not say how the texture reads under lighting or what is painted outside the sampled UV boxes.

silhouette.units: metres; x relative to the midline; z absolute. Divide by heightM for H-fractions (also given as *Frac).
silhouette.torsoRule: Per band, surface samples (vertices plus triangle-edge points, <= H/400 apart) are folded about the midline (|x - midline|), sorted, and split wherever consecutive values differ by more than 0.0075 H (0.0131 m here). The torso cluster is the first run with >= 3 samples; samples beyond it are the arms (lateral*). Above the armpit apex (armsMerged = true, up to the neck) arm and torso are connected, so the torso arrays there report the merged silhouette and are an upper bound. T-pose exception: when no band shows an arm gap and the half-width profile is a step (arms level with the shoulders), bands whose half-width is >= 1.5 x the shoulder half-width (read one band above the arm) are cut at 1.05 x the shoulder half-width (armTrimmed = true), so the arms are excluded. Below the crotch the cluster is both legs together.

head.basis: skin-mesh vertices above the chin (no hair); withAllMeshesBounds adds every mesh in the file above the chin within 1.1 head widths of the midline

face.coordinateSystem: x=(X-midline)/headWidth, y=(Y-chin)/headHeight (0 chin, 1 head top), z=(Z-headBackZ)/headDepth

symmetry.basis: mean distance from each vertex's mirror image about the head midline to the nearest vertex; per-feature errors are in features[].symmetry

noseTip.basis: max-z vertex of the skin mesh in the central face column (|x-midline| <= 0.15 head widths) between the chin and the eye line

layout.basis: eye = the widest paired detail mesh (see inferred.faceFeatureRoles); eye line = its bbox centre height; face width = skin-mesh x extent within +-0.5% H of the eye line

thirds.hairlineNote: the hair fringe's lower edge is at or below the brow line, so the hairline-to-brow third is not measurable (the brows are covered or level with the hair)
thirds.basis: brow = centre of the brow-role detail mesh; nose = max-z skin vertex in the central column; hairline = lowest vertex of the hair-like mesh in the front-central column above the eye line

atlas.textureCoordinateConvention: glTF: origin top-left, v grows downward; pixel row = v * height

faceUv.basis: UV bounding box of the largest mesh island among the skin vertices that are above the chin, in the front half of the head; other islands (eyeball-like pieces, hair-cap) are in regions.face.islands

colours.note: sRGB values 0-255; L* is CIE 1976 from linearised sRGB (D65). `box` statistics include every texel inside the UV bounding box (neighbouring islands, painted features); `vertexSampled` uses only the texel under each region vertex's UV and is the better skin-colour estimate. face = dominant face island, body = skin vertices below the neck.

regions.headStartBasis: narrowest p98(|x|) band of the skin mesh between 0.80H and 0.95H; head starts at that band's upper edge
regions.crotchBasis: highest 0.01H band below 0.58H whose skin vertices leave the centre line (|x|<0.004H) empty, i.e. the legs have separated
regions.armBasis: 1.15 x p98(|x|) of the 0.01H bands 0.05H-0.15H below the crotch (leg/hip half-width, clear of hands at hip height), floor 0.075H
regions.definition: head: y>=headStart; arm: |x|>armHalfWidth; leg: y<crotch; torso: the rest (arm test precedes leg/torso)

quadPairing.definition: two triangles pair when their shared edge is the longest edge of both; near-planar = dihedral < 5 degrees; quad-like = planar and every merged-quad angle in 60-120 degrees

density.bandDefinition: 20 equal bands of figure height; vertices by position, area by triangle centroid, edges by midpoint

regions.definition: vertex region from its position, triangle region from its centroid, edge region from its midpoint (see regions)

uvMirroring.definition: pairs are welded vertices whose x-mirror partner lies within 0.5 mm; shared = any copy has the same UV, mirrored = same v and u+u' equal to one constant, else independent

uvAtlas.atlasSizeSource: embedded PNG/JPEG header of the material's base-colour image

seams.definition: welded-by-position edges whose two sides carry different UV coordinates (open mesh boundaries are not seams)

coverage.samplingNote: pixel-centre point sampling with a fixed jitter; unbiased in aggregate, so small triangles are not rounded up to whole pixels

0.note: pixel claimed by the first mesh rasterised; overlap counted when a later triangle hits an occupied pixel

masks.weldingNote: mask value per welded vertex = max over raw copies; copies differing by >1e-4 are counted per mask as seamInconsistentVertices
masks.relativeFrameDefinition: centroidHeadRelative / centroidTorsoRelative = (centroid - box centre) / box size per axis, box = bbox of the skin vertices in that region; 0 is the box centre, +-0.5 its faces; x is character-left positive

protectedZeros.regionDefinition: skin vertices within 8 mm of any vertex of the small head-band parts (face-detail guess)

scalp.binning: 24 azimuth x 6 equal-solid-angle elevation bins above the head-box centre; a bin is covered when a hair vertex or triangle centroid lies 0.95x..skull radius+10 cm out along it

roots.rootDefinition: per component: the end of its principal axis nearer the head-box centre (mean of the end 8% of vertices); non-elongated components use their vertex nearest the head centre

layering.structure: every garment/accessory is a SEPARATE mesh object floating over a single skin mesh
layering.basis: roles come from geometry only (distance to the skin surface, position in the figure, size); see inferred.roles for each rule

inferred.roles_note: geometry-only guesses; inventory uses name/geometry heuristics too, not authoritative artist labels

subdivision.irregularVertexCountNote: interior vertices with valence other than 4 or 6; not an estimate of the original control-cage vertex count without a known refinement algorithm
subdivision.verdict: valence statistics are consistent with a regular refinement lattice: 83.3% of interior vertices have valence 6 and every irregular vertex sits only among valence-6 neighbours; 37.6% of welded vertices are exact (2 um) midpoints of two triangle-graph neighbours; this adjacency statistic cannot establish or exclude linear subdivision, smoothing or projection. Triangulated quad refinement and diagonal choices change the neighbour pairs; consult authoring source
subdivision.basis: regular lattice = interior valence-6 share >= 0.80 AND >= 95% of non-6 interior vertices have only valence-6 neighbours; midpointMajority = >= 60% of welded vertices lie within 2 um of the midpoint of two triangle-graph neighbours. Neither statistic determines construction history: regular grids, quad triangulation and different refinements can overlap. The original cage and modifier stack are not stored in the GLB; linearSubdivision remains null.

faceStructure.basis: pairedTriangleShare=0.66331; this measures exported triangles, not original quads or authoring history; planarity is reported separately

geometricSymmetry.basis: all-vertex p95 mirror error <= 1.0 mm => symmetric; median <= 1 mm but p95 larger => local deviations; arms compared with the rest at 2x p95

uvSymmetry.layout: mirrored halves share one UV layout (overlapping)
uvSymmetry.basis: sharedUvShare=0.98654, mirroredUvShare=0.0 over matched mirror pairs

atlasUse.basis: coveredPixelShare=0.197 (>=0.6 dense, >=0.3 moderate); overlap share of covered pixels 0.975 (>0.01 = overlapping layout)

normalisation.basis: maximum summed mask value at vertices where >=2 masks are non-zero is 0.94055; <=1 means overlapping regions share rather than stack weight

smoothness.basis: max |delta mask| / edge length over welded edges touching the mask support; a hard-edged mask would show a gradient of 1/edge_length

hair.clumpNote: median component width 64 mm: each component is a thick clump/lock, not an individual hair strand; the true strand count is not recoverable from this mesh
hair.basis: each connected component (welded by position) is measured on its principal axes (length L1 >= width L2 >= thickness L3); tube = L1/L2>=3 and L3/L2>=0.45; ribbon = L3/L2<0.25, L1/L2>=4 and >=24 triangles; card = L3/L2<0.25 otherwise; shell = a dominant low-aspect closed component; the type is the class holding most triangles. Counts are components, so strands merged at the root count as one.

limits: all roles are geometry-only guesses; names, materials and node hierarchy are not used except for the body-mesh ranking and atlas lookup
garment clearance uses stored bind-pose skin positions (static meshes use rest-world transforms); no skin animation was evaluated, so this is not a runtime clearance result
clearance is measured from the garment vertices to the skin only; garment-over-garment offsets are reported as contacts, not distances
density regions (head/torso/arm/leg) come from silhouette heuristics on the skin mesh, not from the skeleton; the upper arm near the shoulder falls into 'torso'
valence and exact-midpoint statistics describe exported connectivity only; they do not identify subdivision, smoothing, projection or the original control cage
UV coverage uses a 256x256 point-sampled raster; overlap below that resolution (sub-pixel overlap) is not detected
texture CONTENT (paint, skin tones, makeup) is not analysed: only UV layout and the image size are
no animation was evaluated: weights and masks are read at the bind pose
